title: Introduce randomized counterfactual probe and soft-fail CI adapter
author: Ava Chen
description: Adds a randomized counterfactual probe to the eval-harness and a soft-fail CI adapter that surfaces regressions without hard-blocking merges unless they exceed configurable statistical thresholds. Motivation: many regressions are brittle to minor prompt edits; counterfactual probing produces small, semantically preserving edits and measures sensitivity. Design: probe generator implements configurable perturbation strategies (entity swap, tense shift, negation flip, punctuation perturbation) with deterministic seeding for reproducibility. The CI adapter runs a small batched probe set against the PR head, computes a bootstrap-based p-value and effect-size estimate, and returns either OK, WARN, or FAIL based on thresholds. WARN is marked as a soft-failure that appears prominently in PR checks and in the console, encouraging fixes without stopping fast-moving teams. Includes CLI flags --counterfactual-seed, --cf-soft-fail-threshold, --cf-min-samples and an autoscaling backoff that reduces probe size when CI concurrency is high. Ties into existing eval telemetry to record sensitivity_score per-prompt and cohort, enabling later alerting and triage. Backwards compatibility: the adapter is opt-in via .eval-config or pipeline flag and defaults to disabled for release branches. Risk: false positives for very small cohorts are mitigated by bootstrap confidence intervals and a minimum-sample guard. Linked work: ENG-4217 for probe design and ENG-4218 for CI adapter integration. Usage: run `eh run --probe counterfactual --seed 1234` locally or rely on the GitHub workflow `counterfactual-smoke.yml` which is added in this PR.

release_notes: Add counterfactual probing and soft-fail CI adapter: opt-in eval check that flags sensitivity regressions using randomized counterfactual edits. Defaults are conservative; enable via .eval-config. See docs/eval/counterfactual-probes.md for usage and tuning.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: probe generation is deterministic with seed, adapter is opt-in, and thresholds are tuned to reduce false positives. It enables later automation to pin problematic prompts into a quarantine cohort for targeted fixes.
